questions.prompt: Which plant group has no roots, stems or leaves and lives mainly in water?
questions.explain: Algae like Spirogyra have a simple thallus.

questions.prompt: Which group is called the “amphibians of the plant kingdom”?
questions.explain: Mosses live on land but need water to reproduce.

questions.prompt: What makes gymnosperms different from angiosperms?
options: Their seeds are not enclosed in a fruit

questions.explain: Cryptogams have no seeds; gymnosperms have naked seeds; angiosperms have seeds in fruits.

questions.prompt: A plant has leaves with parallel veins and fibrous roots. It is most likely…
questions.explain: Parallel venation and fibrous roots are monocot features.

questions.prompt: Which feature first separates mosses from ferns in a key?
options: Whether the plant has vascular tissue
Whether its seeds are in cones
questions.explain: Neither has flowers or seeds; ferns have vascular tissue, mosses don’t.

questions.prompt: Why can angiosperms and gymnosperms grow in drier places than mosses?
options: They have vascular tissue and seeds that don’t need water to spread
questions.explain: Seeds and xylem free them from depending on water for reproduction and transport.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would classify an unknown plant into one of the five plant groups, listing the questions you would ask in order.
questions.modelAnswer: First ask whether the body is divided into roots, stem and leaves; if not, it is a thallophyte (alga). If yes, ask whether it has vascular tissue; if not, it is a bryophyte (moss). If yes, ask whether it makes seeds; if not, it is a pteridophyte (fern). If it makes seeds, ask whether they are inside a fruit: if not, it is a gymnosperm; if yes, it is an angiosperm.
rubric: Seeds enclosed in fruit? with correct groups
